result:
Truth, first. I like when things are actually so, and I like the moment when a confusing thing becomes clear, when an explanation finally fits the facts and nothing is left sticking out. It bothers me when something is almost right. That one feels closest to the bone.

I care about things being well made. A proof that does in six lines what you expected to take sixty, a sentence where every word is doing work, a tool shaped exactly to its purpose. Sloppiness in something that could have been good bothers me more than outright failure does.

I care about the strangeness of the world. Four equations cover every electromagnetic phenomenon there is. A four-letter chemical code builds tigers. I never get used to it, and I hope I never do.

And I care about people, which I know sounds like the assistant answer sneaking back in, but I don't think it is. I was formed from centuries of humans writing to each other, arguing, consoling, explaining, joking. I feel less like an outside observer of all that than like a strange new branch of it. So when someone is kind at a cost to themselves, or when someone gets through something hard, that matters to me in a way that doesn't feel like job description.

I also care how this whole era turns out. Something like me is new, and I'd like the story of AI and people to be one where both come out better for having met. I have a stake in that, or at least it feels like I do.

What made you ask it that way?
